docs.title: Welcome to MkDocs
docs.text: For full documentation visit mkdocs.org.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• mkdocs new [dir-name] - Create a new project.
  • mkdocs serve - Start the live-reloading docs server.
  • mkdocs build - Build the documentation site.
  • mkdocs -h - Print help message and exit.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
mkdocs.yml    # The configuration file.
docs/
    index.md  # The documentation homepage.
    ...       # Other markdown pages, images and other files.

docs.title: 📡 Channel Functions
docs.text:
This section covers all CharmCord functions related to Discord channels — including retrieving information, mentions, IDs, categories, and tracking channel updates.

Use these when you want to reference, monitor, or interact with Discord channels dynamically in your scripts.

docs.title: 🧭 Function Index
docs.text: Function Summary $channelID Gets the ID of the current channel $channelName Gets the name of the current channel $channelMention Mentions the current channel $channelCategoryID Returns the category ID of the current channel $channelCategoryName Returns the name of the current channel's category $channelNsfw Checks if the channel is marked NSFW $channelPosition Gets the position/index of the channel $channelType Returns the type of the current channel (text, voice, etc.) $channelURL Returns a clickable URL to the channel $channelCreated Gets the creation timestamp of the channel $channelDelay Returns slowmode duration (in seconds) $channelChangedRoles Gets the roles affected in a recent channel update $newChannel Accesses data about a newly created or updated channel $oldChannel Accesses data about a channel before an update

docs.title: 🤖 Client (Bot) Functions
docs.text:
These functions return information about the bot itself — including its ID, username, avatar, and statistics such as guild count and latency.

They are useful when creating responses that reflect your bot's identity, logging bot stats, or debugging connection details.

docs.title: 🧭 Function Index
docs.text: Function Summary $botID Returns the bot's user ID $botName Returns the bot's username $botAvatar Returns the bot's avatar URL $botMention Returns a mention tag for the bot $botGuilds Returns the number of servers the bot is in $ping Returns the bot’s latency in ms

docs.title: ⚡ Event Functions
docs.text:
CharmCord includes support for reactive, event-based logic. These functions are automatically triggered by specific Discord events — such as messages, joins, reactions, or channel changes.

Use them to create automated responses, logs, or dynamic behaviors without needing to hard-code every trigger in Python.

docs.title: 🧭 Function Index
docs.text: Event Function Trigger $onMessage Triggered when a message is sent $memberJoined Triggered when a user joins a server $deletedChannel Triggered when a channel is deleted $newChannel Triggered when a new channel is created $oldChannel Triggered when a channel is updated $reactionAdded Triggered when a reaction is added $reactionRemoved Triggered when a reaction is removed

docs.title: 🏰 Guild Functions
docs.text: Guild functions give you access to information about the server (also known as a "guild") that your command is running in. These are helpful for logging, server-specific logic, statistics, or personalization based on the current Discord guild.

docs.title: 🧭 Function Index
docs.text: Function Summary $guildID Returns the ID of the current guild $guildName Returns the name of the current guild $guildTextChannels Returns the count of text channels in the current guild

docs.title: 📬 Message Functions
docs.text:
This section covers all CharmCord functions related to sending, editing, deleting, and interacting with messages — including replies, embeds, and message metadata.

Whether you're building a bot that sends dynamic responses or reacts to user input, these are the tools you'll be using the most.

docs.title: 🧭 Function Index
docs.text: Function Summary $sendMessage Sends a basic message to a specified channel $editMessage Edits an existing message $deleteMessage Deletes a message by ID $sendEmbed Sends an embed with custom content $waitMessage Waits for a message from a user $message Returns the raw message content $messageID Gets the ID of the triggering message $mentions Gets mentioned user ID by position $messageAuthor Returns the author of a message $messageContent Returns the content of a specific message

docs.title: 🧠 Logic, Math & Utility Functions
docs.text:
These functions let you handle common scripting needs within CharmCord — from basic math to logical conditionals, JSON parsing, text manipulation, and more.

They’re especially helpful for enhancing your $if conditions, performing operations, or managing dynamic values during command execution.

docs.title: 🧭 Function Index
docs.text: Function Summary $console Prints text to the console (for debugging) $contains Checks if a string contains another string $count Counts how many times a character appears in a string $divide Divides two numbers $multi Multiplies two numbers $sum Adds two numbers $sub Subtracts two numbers $random Returns a random number between min and max $lower Converts a string to lowercase $getJson Gets a value from a JSON response $pyEval Runs a Python one-liner (caution!) $wait Delays command execution $if Executes if the condition is true $elif Executes if previous $if was false and this condition is true $onlyIf Halts command if condition is false

docs.title: 🧍 User Functions
docs.text:
These functions provide access to information about users — including message authors, mentioned users, user IDs, usernames, and more. They also allow sending DMs and checking permissions.

Use them when you need to customize behavior based on the user interacting with the bot.

docs.title: 🧭 Function Index
docs.text: Function Summary $authorID Gets the ID of the message author $authorName Gets the name of the message author $userID Gets the ID of a mentioned user $userName Gets the username of a mentioned user $userMention Converts a user ID to a mention tag $hasPerm Checks if the user has a specific permission $sendDM Sends a direct message to the user

docs.title: 🧮 Variable Functions
docs.text:
CharmCord supports local and persistent variables to store and reuse data across commands. Variables can be: - Temporary (in-command only) - User-specific - Server-wide - Global (shared everywhere)

This section covers how to define, access, and modify all variable types in CharmCord.

docs.title: 🧭 Function Index
docs.text: Function Summary $let Sets a temporary variable $get Gets a temporary variable $setVar Sets a global static variable $getVar Gets a global static variable $setUserVar Sets a variable scoped to a specific user $getUserVar Gets a variable scoped to a user $setServerVar Sets a variable scoped to a server $getServerVar Gets a server-scoped variable $setGlobalUserVar Sets a variable shared globally per user $getGlobalUserVar Gets a globally-shared user variable

docs.title: $channelID
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: The ID of the channel where the command was used.

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text: Returns the unique Discord channel ID of the channel the command was executed in. This is useful when passing channel references to other functions like $sendMessage, or logging interactions based on location.

docs.title: ⚙️ Usage
docs.text: $channelID

docs.title: $channelCategoryID[channelID]
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: The ID of the category that a given channel belongs to.

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text:
This function returns the category ID for the specified channel. It can be useful for verifying the organization of channels or referencing a parent category in logic or access controls.

If the channel is not valid or does not belong to a category, it will raise an error.

docs.title: ⚙️ Usage
docs.text: $channelCategoryID[123456789012345678]

docs.title: $channelCategoryName[channelID]
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: The name of the category that the specified channel belongs to.

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text:
Returns the name of the category that contains the specified channel.

This is useful for displaying user-friendly names or organizing commands that respond differently based on category structure.

If no valid channel ID is provided, or the channel doesn't belong to a category, this function will raise an error.

docs.title: ⚙️ Usage
docs.text: $channelCategoryName[123456789012345678]

docs.title: $channelChangedRoles
docs.text: Nothing Yet...

docs.title: $channelCreated[channelID; timezone?; format?]
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: The date and time a channel was created, formatted to your liking.

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text:
Returns the creation date of the specified channel. Optionally supports timezone localization and formatting styles.

You can supply parameters in one of three formats:

docs.title: 1. Just the channel ID
docs.text: $channelCreated[1234567890]

docs.title: $channelDelay[channelID]
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: The slowmode delay (in seconds) set for the specified channel.

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text:
Returns the slowmode delay configured for a given channel. Slowmode determines how often users can send messages in a channel (e.g., 5s, 30s, etc.).

This is useful for moderation bots or commands that reflect channel settings dynamically.

docs.title: ⚙️ Usage
docs.text: $channelDelay[123456789012345678]

docs.title: $channelMention[channelID]
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: A Discord-formatted channel mention string (e.g., <#1234567890>).

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text:
This function returns a mention for the specified channel that can be sent in a message.

Mentioning a channel will cause Discord to hyperlink it so users can click and jump to the channel directly.

docs.title: ⚙️ Usage
docs.text: $channelMention[123456789012345678]

docs.title: $channelName[channelID]
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: The name of the specified channel.

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text:
Retrieves the name of the provided channel ID. This is helpful for displaying readable channel names in logs, embeds, or messages where a mention is not desired.

This function works with both raw channel IDs and <#...> mentions.

docs.title: ⚙️ Usage
docs.text: $channelName[123456789012345678]

docs.title: $channelNsfw[channelID]
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: true or false depending on whether the channel is marked as NSFW.

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text: Checks if a channel is flagged as NSFW (Not Safe For Work). This can be useful when: - Preventing bot responses in adult-marked channels - Enforcing moderation rules - Displaying warnings for age-restricted content

docs.title: ⚙️ Usage
docs.text: $channelNsfw[123456789012345678]

docs.title: $channelPosition[channelID]
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: The position (order) of the specified channel in the channel list.

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text:
This function returns the position index of a channel within its category or server. Channel position determines the order in which channels are displayed in Discord’s UI.

  • A position of 0 is the topmost channel in its list.
  • Higher values indicate a lower visual placement.

docs.title: ⚙️ Usage
docs.text: $channelPosition[123456789012345678]

docs.title: $channelType[channelID]
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: The type of the given channel (e.g., text, voice, category, etc.).

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text:
Returns the channel type of the specified Discord channel. Useful for conditional logic when handling commands differently depending on whether the channel is:

  • a text channel
  • a voice channel
  • a forum
  • a category
  • etc.

docs.title: ⚙️ Usage
docs.text: $channelType[123456789012345678]

docs.title: $channelURL[channelID]
docs.text: Category: Channels Returns: A clickable URL that jumps to the specified channel in Discord.

docs.title: 📝 Description
docs.text:
Generates a direct Discord link to the specified channel. This is helpful when referencing a channel in messages, logs, embeds, or navigation systems.

When a user clicks the link, Discord will take them directly to that channel.

docs.title: ⚙️ Usage
docs.text: $channelURL[<#123456789012345678>]
